article_text:
Cineverse is teaming with Trevor Henderson , the horror creator behind viral characters like Siren Head and Cartoon Cat, to adapt his podcast “Mayfair Watchers Society” into a feature film, Variety can reveal exclusively.

Launched in 2022 as part of Cineverse’s Bloody FM network, the “Mayfair Watchers Society” podcast is “presented as a collection of found tapes and audio accounts, each episode focusing on different residents encountering Henderson’s iconic style of monsters,” according to an official description. The film will be a found footage anthology following different stories and creatures from the podcast, including “The Needle,” “Creekman,” “Owls with Teeth,” “Mr. Bag,” “Anxious Dogs,” “Scissors” and “The Clatter.”

Related Stories

Universal Music Group Hit With Layoffs, Several Senior Execs to Leave Company

Henderson is set to produce the “Mayfair” movie and be part of the writing team.

Popular on Variety

“The Cineverse and Bloody Disgusting teams have been great partners on the podcast, and I’ve long been impressed with the film side of the company, and its indie philosophy,” Henderson said. “I look forward to being very hands-on with adapting the podcast into a feature, and look forward to working closely with them as we develop the film, select the directing and writing teams, and get closer to bringing this to fans.”

Henderson has been one of the major benefactors of Hollywood’s rush towards digitally native IP, spurred on by the success of A24’s $400 million hit “Backrooms.” Rights to Henderson’s Siren Head, a mysterious urban predator disguised as a towering siren post, went to Warner Bros. after a competitive bidding war and is now getting the big-screen treatment from director Brian Duffield and screenwriter Zach Cregger. Just a few weeks later, TriStar Pictures scooped up the rights to Henderson’s Cartoon Cat for a feature adaptation.

Cineverse is the genre studio behind films like “Terrifier 3,” “The Toxic Avenger” remake and “Silent Night, Deadly Night.” Recent releases include the 20th anniversary presentation of Guillermo del Toro’s “Pan’s Labyrinth,” which hit theatres Oct. 8.

Trevor Henderson is represented by Verve, Redshift and Marios Rush. The deal was negotiated by Macias and Cineverse VP Creative Development and Filmmaker Relations Steven Peros.

article_text:
Sudanese filmmaker Mohamed Kordofani , whose debut feature “Goodbye Julia” premiered in Cannes’ Un Certain Regard sidebar, has attracted a raft of partners for his follow-up “About Love & September Laws,” which he’ll be taking to Rome’s MIA Market, running from Oct. 19-23.

Produced by Klozium Studios, the production outfit he launched in 2020 with “Goodbye Julia” co-producer Khalid Awad, the film will reunite the core creative team behind Kordofani’s acclaimed debut, including co-producers Marc Irmer, of France’s Dolce Vita; Michael Henrichs, of German production company DGS; and Issraa Elkogali, of Sweden’s RiverFlower. Also on board are “Goodbye Julia” cinematographer Pierre De Villiers, editor Heba Osman, sound designer Rana Eid and co-writer Khaled Alwaleed.

Related Stories

“About Love & September Laws” is the second installment in a planned trilogy that tells the modern history of Sudan. Set in 1983, it follows an African American journalist, Carter, who arrives in Khartoum on a mission to revive a struggling newspaper. There he reunites with Nouri, an old friend he hasn’t seen in 10 years, now an idealistic doctor who serves as an ideological counterpoint to the jaded reporter.

Things grow complicated when Carter falls for Fatin, his newly hired translator, unaware that she is Nouri’s ex-wife. The fragile romance collides with the sudden weight of politics when Sharia law is imposed across Sudan, and Nouri finds himself facing the death sentence when he refuses a court order to amputate a thief’s hand.

When Carter uncovers a story that could expose the regime’s hypocrisy and save Nouri’s life, he’s forced to choose between the career he came to rebuild, the friendship that gave him a home in Sudan and a love he is only beginning to realize he can’t afford to lose.

Speaking to Variety ahead of MIA, Kordofani explains that while “About Love & September Laws” is set against the backdrop of a pivotal moment in Sudanese history, at its core “it’s a story about three people who are entangled in different kinds of love.”

The director’s groundbreaking debut was the first Sudanese feature to make the official selection at the Cannes Film Festival. Executive produced by Academy Award winner Lupita N’yongo, the film won the Un Certain Regard section’s Freedom Prize along with 65 other international plaudits, including audience awards at El Gouna and Singapore. In a rave review , Variety ’s Jessica Kiang praised the “engrossing” drama as a “well-performed deep cut into Sudan’s recent history [that] unfolds like a morality thriller.”

As with “Goodbye Julia,” which takes place in Khartoum during the six years prior to the 2011 secession of South Sudan, Kordofani’s latest again looks to “bridge the personal and the political, the local and the global, the past and the present,” he says. However, after his first feature struggled to break into the U.S. and U.K. markets, the director says he’s determined to “reach even wider audiences.”

“Even before ‘Goodbye Julia,’ I’ve always wanted to make films that are for the mainstream but still hold artistic value, educational value — [sharing] something about my country that people don’t know,” he says. “I still want to do the things I want to do, but I want to make the film more accessible. The wider the reach, the better.”

Last December, “About Love & September Laws” scooped a trio of prizes at the Red Sea Film Festival’s industry Souk Awards. In Rome, where it’s among the 12 projects taking part in MIA’s Film Co-Production Market, Kordofani said he’s particularly “looking for partners that can [build a] bridge to the United States.”

“It’s a film with an American lead. It’s predominantly English. I think, in the development stage, I should start building these bridges, not only for casting but also for the journey of the film and presenting the film [to a U.S. audience],” he says.

Central to that will be the lead role of Carter, a former Black Panther and disillusioned reporter who’s “lost faith in bigger causes and bigger movements,” says Kordofani. Opposite him is Nouri, the idealistic doctor, whose refusal to enforce a Sharia court order puts his life in jeopardy. “There’s this clash of personalities,” says the director, characterizing the film as a “moral drama” where “slowly, the politics will seep into their story and guide how the story unfolds.”

A winner of Variety ’s MENA Talent of the Year Award in 2023, Kordofani is among the many Sudanese who were forced to flee the country amid the ongoing war. Now based in Nairobi, where he and Awad have established their production shingle Klozium Studios, he nevertheless feels an obligation to his homeland, saying, “I do feel a responsibility to talk about Sudan.”

“Living apart from my family, I continue to…search for purpose through filmmaking,” he says. “And especially now, as war rages on, I feel an urgent responsibility to preserve and create our own narrative — before it is stolen, silenced or rewritten by others.”

“About Love & September Laws,” he adds, offers “a platform to engage directly with the Western world, not as an outsider telling Sudan’s story, but as someone inviting them into a shared conversation about freedom, sacrifice, love and truth-seeking.”

article_text:
Natasha Lennard’s ‘On Un/Certainty’ wonders what to make of the very notion of certainty, and whether the best course of action is refusal

Today we are frequently told, as the British-born, New York-based academic Natasha Lennard reminds us in On Un/Certainty , that ‘we live in uncertain times’ – and of course, across multiple related metrics, from developments in AI to climate change to geopolitics, we do. But this invocation of uncertainty, along with talk of crisis and polycrisis, serves the needs of power in that it suggests a reality founded on doubt, a reality that is, per the documentarian Adam Curtis, too complex to process. Meanwhile, myriad bad actors and flat-out neofascists are acting in absolute ideological certainty. US cops shoot Black civilians in the certainty that they can walk free after claiming self-defence. ICE officers and politicians enact the certainty that open borders and migration are bad things, empowered in turn by both racism and the certainty that immigrants are, Lennard writes, ‘a reliable scapegoat for working-class economic pain’. Politicians declared, against the uncertainties of COVID, that the pandemic was over, endorsing the certainty that capitalism-as-usual is more important than human life. Anti-trans activists are certain that trans women are not women. Trump’s cuts to science funding are ‘acts of certainty against knowledge’ – which, in turn, will produce uncertainty themselves, for instance, when the next pandemic hits.

Lennard explores all these dualities lucidly, readably and in detail, but to get there she begins with the weaponisation of the very notion of crisis. Crisis, when invoked, is generally authorless and so blameless, so (for example) the genocide in Gaza is framed by news outlets as a ‘humanitarian crisis’, rather than the result of extremely deliberate actions by Israel. AI, meanwhile, has authors (the techbroligarch class) but is framed by them as something like manifest destiny, inevitable, eschatological; the ‘myth of our inevitable replacement’ more important than the waste of natural resources, since what’s at stake is ‘the very survival of humanity’, if not human beings (capitalism would, if it could, do away with human labour, Lennard notes: robots, besides being cheaper, won’t unionise or protest).

All of this is framed within philosophical arguments from Ludwig Wittgenstein’s posthumous 1969 book On Certainty , which explores the extent to which we can be certain: how we can say we know what we know, which turns out to be fairly relativistic, a middle way between knowing and not-knowing. (You can’t ask if there’s wine left in the bottle, Lennard writes by example, if you doubt there’s a bottle.) Beyond philosophicopolitical investigations, though, where do we go? At the outset, Lennard says that what matters, in terms of resistance, is our ‘acts’, a simple enough notion she returns to at the book’s conclusion, allying it to the existential question of how ‘antifascist, liberatory practices’ can be sustained without their proponents falling into exhaustion or apathy. Lennard’s answers are straightforward, fillable, non-revelatory frameworks: general strikes that consist of ‘community care, militant disruption, working-class refusal’; remembering previous times when ‘[w]e have cared for each other, refused complicity, refused to work, worked, taken risks, taught, shared, marched, blockaded, found each other and acted in great numbers’.

This being an art magazine, it’s worth considering how the thematic applies to art. Since modernity, arguably since Cézanne and unquestionably since Duchamp, art has founded itself on bedrock uncertainty, to the point where it has sometimes become a schtick of dense codifications, obscure references, deliberate incoherence. The past decade, though, saw artists pursuing social justice lose patience with uncertainty and want to make statements instead. Of late, in apparent reaction to that, it seems like ambiguity and obscurity are staging a comeback. Yet if uncertainty, as seen through Lennard’s lens, has been coopted by power, what kind of doubt is appropriate to art today? For all its other virtues, this slim volume is as good a place as any to begin asking that question.

On Un/Certainty: The Uses of Doubt in Dangerous Times by Natasha Lennard. Verso , £16.99 (hardcover)

summary_zh: 来源摘录：將於 2026 年 10 月 16 日正式開展的第 33 屆女性影展，以「非分擾動 Into the Drift」為年度視覺，藉由流動、穿梭的視覺意象，向當代持續變動的疆界、關係發出提問，嘗試在一個世紀的電影裡，尋找錨定自身位置，重新想像自由的樣貌。 這篇文章 【編輯室】𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 台灣國際女性影展專題：女人沒有鄉愁 ╳ 編輯室推薦片 最早出現於 釀電影 。

"不同於《莫那岡貝：自由的吶喊》與《桑比贊加》的革命敘事，這部電視電影是莎拉・馬爾多羅少見的輕盈喜劇。巧妙翻轉高級料理與街頭粗活、法國精英與非洲移民的既定界線，經由一本食譜的輾轉流傳，探問誰能擁有法國文化。當多數電影依然把黑人移工形塑為悲苦受害者，馬爾多羅卻相信歡樂與政治可以共存，不讓壓迫成為黑人生命的唯一定義。雙活寶主角一搭一唱，談吐自帶嘻哈魂，掃地搖擺如跳舞，在笑鬧中活出尊嚴，日常就是他們最靈巧的抵抗。"}, 年代提出「黑人性」（Négritude）的思想巨擘，喚醒長年遭殖民壓抑的黑人文化意識，重新擁抱自身歷史。電影隨其出席國際交流、漫步家鄉、朗讀詩作、暢談理念，回望如何用文字實踐民族解放。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": Maldoror，1929－2020），本次也將收錄獨立評論人黃曦，自多部經典電影爬梳女性主義與反殖民運動、去殖民途徑的抵抗力量。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "延續關於時間、時代之思索，本專題另有三篇獨立評論，分別由獨立評論人許騰云、小說家趙鴻祐與新銳評論人黎思行執筆。透過普拉迪・克里申（Pradip Krishen）《安尼閣來舞這齣》（In Which 撰文／黃曦 劇照提供／台灣國際女性影展 專題作者／黃曦、趙鴻祐、許騰云、陳穎、黎思行

2026 台灣國際女性影展「焦點影人」單元，莎拉．馬爾多羅（Sarah Maldoror）。／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展（© B.J. Nikolaisen）

❏ 焦點影人單元：莎拉．馬爾多羅（Sarah Maldoror）

黑人女性導演先驅莎拉・馬爾多羅（1929－2020），以反殖民經典《桑比贊加》，成為世界女性電影史與非洲電影史的重要一頁，也讓他被冠上「非洲電影之母」或「革命電影作者」等稱號。然而真正走近作品，會發現這些標籤既正確也不足。

一生創作四十餘部作品，創作軌跡緊貼 20 世紀重要社會思潮與政治運動──黑人性、反殖民、泛非主義、女性主義等，回應當前最迫切的需求與渴望，不懈記錄人民爲追尋平等與自由迸發的生命吶喊。透過這次選映的 12 部作品，從革命到日常，從劇情、紀錄到詩性表現，梳理出馬爾多羅如何用影像實踐自由與反抗，並藉此洞見其作品的豐富樣貌。

《莫那岡貝：自由的吶喊》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➀《莫那岡貝：自由的吶喊》Monangambééé，1969）

一名安哥拉政治犯遭殖民政府監禁，妻子探監時說下次帶來「完整套餐」，竟被獄卒誤認為革命暗號。一個尋常用語，瞬間引爆猜忌，招來殘酷審訊刑求。這場因誤解而生的悲劇，徹底暴露殖民者對當地文化跟語言的無知，並揭示恐懼作為暴力的根源。

本片為莎拉・馬爾多羅首部執導作品，已顯現日後鮮明風格：捨棄革命電影慣見的英雄稱頌、激烈戰鬥與直白說教，而是從女性視角、受難者身體與日常經驗出發，將抗爭意志凝練為詩性影像。片名意指安哥拉解放戰士的集結口號，由美國芝加哥藝術合奏團「Art Ensemble of Chicago」演奏的前衛配樂，在爆裂與寂靜之間游移，宛如另一具受迫而不屈的身體，讓非洲反殖民與美國黑人解放運動，於自在節拍下跨洋共振。

《桑比贊加》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➁《桑比贊加》（Sambizanga，1972）

1961 年安哥拉獨立戰爭爆發前夕，一名拖拉機司機忽然被秘密警察粗暴逮捕，送入首都監獄。妻子見丈夫下落不明，揹著襁褓中的嬰孩四處尋找。從鄉村到城市、從家門到獄門，這趟尋夫之旅也串起一場蓄勢待發的民族解放運動。

莎拉・馬爾多羅首部劇情長片，與伴侶馬里奧・德安德拉德（Mário Raul de Morais Andrade，1893－1945，安哥拉人民解放運動領袖）共同編劇。片名意指首都的一個工人階級社區，居民正為起義醞釀，準備攻打監獄劫囚。電影拍攝時，安哥拉仍深陷獨立戰爭泥淖，然而片中不見直接的革命呼籲、陽剛的戰鬥場面，反而以女性的積極奔走為軸，交織鄰里的隱密互助，在日常中形塑抵抗。

《狗兒沉默著》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➂《狗兒沉默著》（And the Dogs Were Silent，1978）

改編艾梅・塞澤爾（Aimé Fernand David Césaire，1913－2008）的同名詩劇，內容關於一名革命者在赴死前的長串獨白，以及跟母親的對話。馬爾多羅大膽將舞台搬進巴黎人類博物館的倉庫，場景擺滿殖民時代掠奪的黑人文物，讓反殖民尺度回溯至奴隸制年代，並擴及藝術典藏與知識生產層面。

《垃圾桶裡的美味秘方》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➃《垃圾桶裡的美味祕方》（A Dessert for Constance，1979）

兩名來自非洲的清潔工，在巴黎街頭的垃圾桶，意外撿到一本 19 世紀的法式料理食譜。為了替病重友人籌措返鄉旅費，他們決定報名電視料理益智節目，就算書中食材樣樣吃不起，仍要靠著死背活記，拚命贏得獎金！

不同於《莫那岡貝：自由的吶喊》與《桑比贊加》的革命敘事，這部電視電影是莎拉・馬爾多羅少見的輕盈喜劇。巧妙翻轉高級料理與街頭粗活、法國精英與非洲移民的既定界線，經由一本食譜的輾轉流傳，探問誰能擁有法國文化。當多數電影依然把黑人移工形塑為悲苦受害者，馬爾多羅卻相信歡樂與政治可以共存，不讓壓迫成為黑人生命的唯一定義。雙活寶主角一搭一唱，談吐自帶嘻哈魂，掃地搖擺如跳舞，在笑鬧中活出尊嚴，日常就是他們最靈巧的抵抗。

《艾梅塞澤爾：文字的面具》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➄《艾梅塞澤爾：文字的面具》（Aimé Césaire: The Mask of Words，1987）

影響深遠的黑人知識分子艾梅・塞澤爾，是用文字追尋自由的詩人、法國海外領地馬丁尼克的政治家，更是在 1930 年代提出「黑人性」（Négritude）的思想巨擘，喚醒長年遭殖民壓抑的黑人文化意識，重新擁抱自身歷史。電影隨其出席國際交流、漫步家鄉、朗讀詩作、暢談理念，回望如何用文字實踐民族解放。

這是莎拉・馬爾多羅第二次拍這位精神導師，以介於人物紀錄、散文電影與詩電影之間的獨特形式呈現，也成為側面理解馬爾多羅中晚期創作觀的稜鏡。詩在本片不只被朗誦，還化為影片結構與節奏，探索屬於黑人的感知語彙。片名「面具」源於塞澤爾對自己文字的比喻，並非指涉遮蔽現實，而是如非洲文化的儀式面具，讓他超越個人，與祖先及集體記憶相連。

《萊昂達馬斯：詩之聲》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➅《萊昂達馬斯：詩之聲》（Léon G. Damas，1994）

黑人性（Négritude）運動的三位奠基者中，圭亞那詩人萊昂・達馬斯（Léon-Gontran Damas，1912－1978）的名聲雖不及艾梅・塞澤爾與利奧波德・桑戈爾（Léopold Sédar Senghor，1906－2001）響亮，卻是最早發出憤怒異議的文化先鋒。本片在主題與形式上，接近《艾梅塞澤爾：文字的面具》，但在手法上更加奔放，更趨於散文電影與詩電影，以綿延長河為結構與隱喻，讓詩歌與風景、影像與聲音匯為怒川，向這位被遺忘的拓荒前輩致敬。

《前進米蘭 RAP 上天》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➆《前進米蘭 RAP 上天》（Scala Milan A.C.，2003）

一群熱愛足球的巴黎郊區少年，為了贏得前往義大利米蘭、觀賞愛隊比賽的機會，決定以饒舌表演，角逐社區形象影片競賽，還獲得傳奇樂手亞契・謝普（Archie Shepp）相助。一場球迷夢，逐漸通往遼闊的藝術天地。馬爾多羅延續對黑人社群的關注，讓足球與饒舌、爵士、歌劇相遇，在青春喧鬧中打開新視野。他視孩子為躁動的鳥，渴望用肢體與節拍表達自我，藉此作期盼下一代展翅飛翔。

《野草蔓生》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

❏ 屬於她的遊蕩單元

「無可預期、意料之外的遊蕩」在影史上經常與解放、反叛、自由形象互作聯想。女性無法被定義的遊蕩，進一步複雜化瀟灑、叛逆形象背後的性別運作，以及觀者的凝視。本單元選映三部作者導演完成於 1980、1990 年代的首部劇情長片，皆以女子的遊蕩開展敘事，透過身體在不同空間、地景的移動，映照自身的存在面貌，亦是對既有秩序的全面擾動。

女子的遊蕩本身即是一場向內／外的究極提問，除了三部經典修復片外，亦搭配三部當代作品，推展人的移動與不安於室之於當代社會在意義上的延續與形變，以時空的跨越映照出變化多端的遊蕩狀態。

《里昂的跫音》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➀《里昂的跫音》（Blind Spot，1981）

【導演簡介】克勞迪亞・馮阿萊曼（Claudia von Alemann）：自1960年代開始創作，作品橫跨實驗、紀錄與劇情，首部劇情長片《Blind Spot》被視作女性主義電影經典。1973 年與赫克．桑德爾於西柏林的 Arsenal 兵工廠電影院共同舉辦史上首屆「國際女性電影研討會」。

【劇情簡介】伊莉莎白（Elizabeth）對 19 世紀法國社會主義作家與早期女性主義先驅弗洛拉・特里斯坦（Flore Celestine，1803－1844）的日記深深著迷，決定拋下丈夫、孩子，一人踏上前往里昂的旅行。穿梭在里昂的街道巷弄，他追隨特里斯坦的腳步，試圖透過自身漫遊的跫音，貼近逝者生前的所思所想。當他拒絕以最直觀的方式「觀看」歷史，城市空間在他腳下逐漸鋪展成偌大的回聲室，層疊時空在此交會，帶來未曾想像過的聲響共振。

被遺忘之人如何被記憶？逝去的歷史如何在生者的時空產生共響？逝者的生命經驗能否在當刻觸發某種政治動能？克勞迪亞・馮阿萊曼的首部劇情長片透過女子的漫遊，不斷向「歷史」拋出層層詰問，以身體的移動親驗歷史書寫的侷限與潛能，亦是以女性主義途徑探尋女性歷史的激進嘗試。

《煙硝下的斑斕》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➁《煙硝下的斑斕》（The Razor's Edge，1985）

【導演簡介】喬瑟琳・薩博（Jocelyne Saab）：黎巴嫩紀錄片先驅，大學修讀經濟學，曾任電視新聞記者，1975 年黎巴嫩內戰爆發後，開始以紀錄片記錄戰火下的家鄉。代表作為「貝魯特三部曲」，風格偏向抒情、詩意、私人，被視為散文電影的重要作者。薩博亦為 2019 年女性影展焦點影人。

【劇情簡介】攝於黎巴嫩內戰期間，喬瑟琳・薩博的首部劇情長片以一場不尋常的相遇，映照出戰火下人民對於生活、慾望、自由與藝術的不懈追尋。薩瑪（Sama）是在戰爭中長大的難民女孩，喜歡四處晃蕩；卡里姆（Kareem）則是名中年畫家，試圖在戰火摧殘的生活中尋找創作的意義。看似身處平行世界的兩人，在亂世中相遇，對彼此產生情愫。

延續「貝魯特三部曲」直視家鄉傷痕的視角，本片鏡頭不時在戰火延燒過的斷垣殘壁與常民生活上駐留，呈現以黎巴嫩首都貝魯特（Beyrouth）為主角的另一條敘事軸線。歷經十年戰事的貝魯特承載著愛情故事，人的際遇與城市命運相繫，愛慕絮語化作獻給貝魯特的情書，亦是對戰爭的深沉控訴。本片自 1985 年首映後旋即消失於公眾視野，直到 2025 年修復完成才得以重返大銀幕。

《野草蔓生》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➂《野草蔓生》（River of Grass，1994）

【導演簡介】凱莉・萊卡特（Kelly Reichardt）：美國獨立導演、編劇、剪輯。1994 年以首部劇情長片《野草蔓生》嶄露頭角，作品曾於坎城、柏林、威尼斯等國際影展首映。代表作包括《溫蒂與露西》（Wendy and Lucy，2008）、《屬於她們的片刻》（Certain Women（，2016）、《深夜裡的美味祕方》（First Cow，2019）等。2024 年榮獲坎城影展金馬車獎。

【劇情簡介】寇茲（Kurtz）的婚後生活沉悶而令人窒息，在某次衝動離家後，與無所事事的魯蛇男子搭上線，一同在外四處晃蕩，沒想到一段意外插曲促使他們踏上崎嶇蜿蜒的逃命之旅。有槍、有車、有搭檔，想亡命走天涯，事情卻不如想像簡單。

凱莉・萊卡特首部劇情長片，以年少時居住的佛羅里達南部郊區為背景，平庸的荒蕪地景在 16mm 的鏡頭下展開，彰顯角色存在意義的荒謬與詰問。萊卡特曾形容片中角色是生活黯淡無光的電視世代，腦海中充斥著離經叛道的銀幕形象，卻少了付諸實踐的本事。全片巧妙挪用並翻轉類型元素，打造出一部反向操作的公路電影，如導演所述：「這是一部沒有路的公路電影，沒有愛的愛情故事，沒有犯罪的犯罪電影。」

《相遇皆有痕》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

❏ 行動漣漪單元

本單元收錄的四部作品，皆收束在「人」身在社會中的存在命題。透過檢視並省思生命經驗的方式，梳理個體與社會的狀態。在這些作品中，事件如連續效應般連環緊扣，如輪舞般勾連出人事物之間的關係，帶出層層關卡與際遇之於個體所帶來的烙印與影響。面對不可逆的人生際遇或創傷記憶，角色選擇另闢蹊徑，以非典型路線追本溯源、按圖索驥並積極探問，將已發生的過往紀事轉化爲扎根現在與未來的想像藍圖。

《沒有的派對》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➀《沒有的派對》（Sometimes, I Imagine Them All at a Party，2026）

【導演簡介】丹妮亞拉・麥蘭妮・胡勒（Daniela Magnani Hüller）：1995 年生於慕尼黑，德裔巴西籍導演。德國帕紹大學媒體與傳播學系畢業，後於慕尼黑電視與電影學院修習紀錄片執導。短片作品曾多次入圍國際影展。首部紀錄長片《沒有的派對》於 2026 柏林影展首映。

【劇情簡介】彩色的雲霄飛車軌道上，藍天與綠蔭模糊，天旋地轉，世界在一瞬顛倒。17 歲曾遭班上男同學跟騷、殺害未遂而倖存的導演，十餘載後重新回憶創傷事件。從當年事發的公車站為始，冷靜的口白自述經歷，接著親自尋訪事件相關人物，如學校老師、女同學、醫生、檢察官等。從私人的個案，轉向社會結構問題的討論；從直接施暴的加害者，擴及叩問那些沉默、旁觀的暴力。

本片巧妙地在保有距離的訪問對談，與私密且具身體感的第一人稱旁白間轉換。隧道燈光、遊樂園霓虹、不明色塊穿插片段閃爍的 Super 8 影像與迷你 DV 畫面，如同過去破碎的記憶，也如想像的夢境。致那些受傷、未能倖存的靈魂，這場派對裝載他們未熄的熠熠生命力。

《相遇皆有痕》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➁《相遇皆有痕》（Every Contact Leaves a Trace，2025）

【導演簡介】琳恩・薩克斯（Lynne Sachs）：美國實驗電影導演、詩人，現居紐約。作品融合檔案、日記、書信、詩歌與音樂，以散文電影形式穿梭現實與記憶，探索身體、影像與電影物質性的交會，並從女性主義視角回應歷史、政治與個人經驗。作品曾於紐約現代藝術博物館及日舞影展等重要美術館與影展放映。

【劇情簡介】面對成堆用不到、卻捨不得丟掉的舊名片，導演琳恩・薩克斯可能是最能發掘其中趣味的翹楚。她像一名記憶偵探，循線尋找那些曾在人生某個時刻擦肩而過的人，甚至將名片送進法醫實驗室，檢驗殘留的指紋與 DNA，試圖追尋這些陌生又熟悉的名字。從經歷二戰的德國女性、遭受審查的藝術家，到改變她人生的心理治療師，那些短暫的相遇，又留下了什麼痕跡？

延續其散文電影的敘事風格，巧妙地在紀錄、重演、詩意旁白之間游移。她將法醫學「凡接觸必留痕跡」的概念延伸至情感與記憶，思考每一次相遇如何成為一扇通往個人生命經驗的入口。名片，成為人際關係的延展，層層疊疊交織出一場關於記憶、身分與人際連結的探索旅程。

《安尼閣來舞這齣》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

❏ 複數作用單元

本單元透過四部作品，描繪人與人之間、人與物種之間的聚合，藉由多樣風格的影音部署勾勒複數存在的可能樣貌。從阿根廷的動物園、法國的教育現場、印度的建築系學生生活，再到南韓的街頭集結，這些作品碰觸生命的相互依存、個體與他者的界線，以及生命交織形成的共振共頻。並透過聯合共作掀起集體能量，揭開跨世代、跨物種想像的多元、差異與多音複義。

《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➀《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》（Writing Life – Annie Ernaux Through the Eyes of High School Students，2025）

【導演簡介】克萊兒・西蒙（Claire Simon）：資深法國紀錄片導演。1970 年代投入創作，作品從女性主義視角出發，關注社會結構中的個人經驗，並探索真實與虛構、觀察與介入之間的界線。代表作包括《上帝辦公室》（Les Bureaux de Dieu，2008）、《電影夢的開始》（The Graduation，2016）、《診間的身景》（Notre corps，2023）等，作品多次入選坎城、柏林、威尼斯等國際影展。

【劇情簡介】諾貝爾文學獎得主安妮・艾諾（Annie Ernaux）的文字，如何進入一群法國高中生的生命？導演克萊兒．西蒙走入巴黎近郊、外省與法屬圭亞那（Guyane française）的校園，記錄學生閱讀、討論艾諾作品的過程。他們從階級、家庭、身體、性別與成長經驗出發，重新審視自己的身分與所處的社會。那些關於墮胎、愛情、親情與羞恥的坦白書寫，成為年輕世代探索自我、挑戰既定規範的契機。

本片延續導演對社會制度下的空間與人際互動的關注，未遵循傳統作家紀錄片的傳記式敘事，而以細膩的觀察與對話開展，呈現青少年的想法與情緒流動。將艾諾「自我社會誌」的書寫風格化為一面鏡子，映照不同背景學生的生命經驗，展現文學閱讀如何成為思考世界、理解他人，也重新想像自身位置的力量。

《安尼閣來舞這齣》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

➁《安尼閣來舞這齣》（In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones，1989）

【導演簡介】普拉迪・克里申（Pradip Krishen）：印度導演、自然學家與環境保育者。畢業於牛津大學，早期以電影創作聞名，與妻子、作家阿蘭達蒂・洛伊（Arundhati Roy）共同創作《In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones》（1989）、《Electric Moon》（1992）。1990 年代後轉向自然研究，致力於印度植物生態、原生景觀復育，並出版多部關於樹木與森林的著作。

【劇情簡介】建築系學生安尼（Annie）因多年前嘲諷院長而遭到刁難，眼看畢業考將近，一場對抗權威、尋找出路的青春喜劇就此展開。電影以 1970 年代印度新德里為背景，描繪即將步入社會的新鮮人，在理想與現實之間的掙扎。這群不安現狀的青年談論馬克思主義、思考現代建築的社會責任，面對僵化的教育制度，他們展開行動，在校園生活中追尋理想、友情與自我定位。

知名作家阿蘭達蒂・洛伊取材自身求學經驗，身兼編劇並飾演要角。電影以幽默流暢的敘事，融入流行的西方搖滾樂、左翼思想與反建制精神，呈現一齣帶有荒謬色彩的校園喜劇。原片長期僅透過錄影帶流傳，具 Cult 片地位，經 4K 數位修復重新問世，凸顯其作為印度獨立電影與青年文化經典的歷史價值。

《釀電影》女人沒有鄉愁──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 台灣國際女性影展專題／圖像提供：釀電影

將於 2026 年 10 月 16 日正式開展的第 33 屆女性影展，以「非分擾動 Into the Drift」為年度視覺，藉由流動、穿梭的視覺意象，向當代持續變動的疆界、關係發出提問，嘗試在一個世紀的電影裡，尋找錨定自身位置，重新想像自由的樣貌。

《釀電影》編輯室以「女人沒有鄉愁」為策展專題，延伸「流動」一詞作為觀看當代世界的方法，循著穿行於城市與鄉野、家庭與個體、戰爭與和平之間的選擇，即從無法無家、無法有家，又何處不是家的概念出發，嘗試看見女性在巨大歷史的移動軌跡之中，曾經被隱匿、邊緣的流離。

當「鄉愁」經常性地被放置在傳統父權結構底下，指涉國族敘事框架、血緣根源、既定秩序的眷戀與歸返，自破除疆界而起的遊牧，便關乎於女性電影中的身分、身體、時間與抗爭之路徑。

本次專題委邀 策展人陳慧穎 進行訪問，自「屬於她的遊蕩」單元的六部電影作品展開，重新爬梳半世紀的世界之變，與存於其中的不變；同時亦邀請獨立評論人陳穎，深入分析「屬於她的遊蕩」單元中，三部來自八〇、九〇年代的導演首作，以「移動」與「身體性」為軸，試論空間為性別運動、女性主義所開創的嶄新變革。

圍繞著「跨越」、「移動」的概念，今年的「焦點影人」單元為非裔法國電影導演莎拉・馬羅多羅（Sarah Maldoror，1929－2020），本次也將收錄獨立評論人黃曦，自多部經典電影爬梳女性主義與反殖民運動、去殖民途徑的抵抗力量。

延續關於時間、時代之思索，本專題另有三篇獨立評論，分別由獨立評論人許騰云、小說家趙鴻祐與新銳評論人黎思行執筆。透過普拉迪・克里申（Pradip Krishen）《安尼閣來舞這齣》（In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones，1989）回到七〇年代，與作家阿蘭達蒂・洛伊（Arundhati Roy）進行跨越世代對話；接著隨克萊兒・西蒙（Claire Simon）《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》（Writing Life – Annie Ernaux Through the Eyes of High School Students，2025）與當代學子的對讀，將書寫轉化為面向未來、身分的路徑；最後由琳恩・薩克斯（Lynne Sachs）《相遇皆有痕》（Every Contact Leaves a Trace，2025）的實驗性展開評析，記述散文電影無有時間，卻凝刻空間、記憶的痕跡。

最後，本專題亦與《沒有的派對》（Sometimes, I Imagine Them All at a Party，2026）導演丹妮亞拉・麥蘭妮・胡勒（Daniela Melanie Goode）展開深入對談，自導演十餘年後執起攝影機，透過多重影像媒介將創傷記憶轉化為與公共對話，甚至對抗體制的政治力量，以期提出一種嶄新的、當代的對話空間是──「女人沒有鄉愁」的起點不在故土，而在踏出疆界、凝視創傷、重構語言與時間的游蕩中，我們如何在生命的蜿蜒之中，持續闖蕩？

"与此同时，马哈茂德认为，最大的问题之一甚至在选片人观看投稿之前就已经出现。他认为，电影人往往在没有确定电影节是否适合其作品的情况下就盲目投递。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他指出：“一部探讨社会议题的电影，可能会被投递到一个主要关注环境主题或自然世界的电影节上。“为什么要把一部电影投给一个与其主题或艺术愿景不相符的电影节呢？”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这使得发行策略在电影制作过程中变得越来越核心。“我认为电影发行已经变得与剪辑、摄影、制作和导演同等重要，”马哈茂德接着说道。无论是自己发行作品还是与专业人士合作，他认为电影人应当考虑首映策略、电影节的选片侧重点以及其观众是否适合该片，而不是简单地尽可能广泛地投递。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一旦电影人确定了合适的电影节，马哈茂德指出，一些更基础的错误也可能会毁掉一份投稿。电影人参加了错误的竞赛单元、遗漏了必需的信息或材料、未能回复电影节的要求，或者投递了超出资格期限的电影。“电影人在投递前应该仔细查阅电影节的规则和要求，”他敦促道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "马哈茂德强调：“一部电影入选电影节并不一定意味着它是一部好电影，也不意味着它是最好的电影。相反，一部电影被拒并不意味着它缺乏质量或艺术价值。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "鹿特丹阿拉伯电影节自身的选片侧重点与欧洲主要电影节不同。阿德尔法塔赫估计，其约有一半或更多的节目来自开罗、红海、艾尔古纳、马拉喀什或安曼等阿拉伯电影节，而通过戛纳、柏林或威尼斯获取的电影相对较少。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他还拒绝将阿拉伯电影视为单一整体的观点。“马格里布的电影与埃及的电影不同，”他说，并举例指出了电影在摩洛哥、埃及和黎巴嫩的不同发展路径。“我们共享某些价值观，但我们有着不同类型的电影。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种区别对于同时服务于阿拉伯观众和荷兰观众的电影节至关重要。阿德尔法塔赫表示，鹿特丹的观众在这两群人中大致平分秋色，而电影在不同群体中的反响并不总是完全相同。喜剧尤其具有揭示性。他回忆起在一次放映中，听到房间的两半在不同的时刻发出笑声。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Sharjah-fest-3.jpg?w=1000", "alt": "", "caption": "穆罕默德·马哈茂德、罗什·阿德尔法塔赫、达琳·萨拉姆由亚历山大国际短片电影节、鹿特丹阿拉伯电影节、麦斯·加莫提供", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“翻译是一门困难的艺术，”他说，并指出这一挑战不仅限于语言，还延伸到了文化背景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对马哈茂德而言，电影节对新兴电影人的责任也不应仅限于挑选和展映他们的作品。他认为电影节应当将年轻电影人与成熟的导演和制片人联系起来，同时提供工作坊和大师班，让他们能够提升技能并向已经在业界工作的人学习。“这使得年轻电影人能够学习、建立人脉、获得灵感并在专业上成长，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴勒斯坦裔约旦籍电影人达林·J·萨拉姆（Darin J. Sallam）曾执导《法哈》（“Farha”），也是今年沙迦国际电影节（SIFF）故事片评审团的成员，她从选片流程的另一端来看待电影节的决策。作为一位也曾担任过评审的电影人，她深知个人视角对这些决定有着多大的塑造作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "萨拉姆表示：“评价电影归根结底是一个主观的过程，受到个人视角和审美品味的塑造。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在进行评审时，萨拉姆对比较各种风格或技术成就不太感兴趣，反而更看重放映结束后留下的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她解释说：“这关乎电影人如何处理这些理念，它们如何让我们作为评审团成员产生共鸣，以及当我们在第二天醒来时，哪些角色和故事依然留在我们的记忆中。对我而言，一部电影的成功与否，与它在放映结束后如何在人们的心中继续存活有关。”", "translated": true}]

article_text:
A film festival selection or rejection is not necessarily a verdict on a film’s quality. For programmers sorting through hundreds or even thousands of submissions, the decision can depend on everything from the balance of a lineup to the audience for which they are programming.

That issue was at the center of “Film Festivals Decoded: What Happens After You Press Submit?,” a panel held this week during the 13th Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth in the UAE. Variety spoke further with two of its participants, Rotterdam Arab Film Festival artistic director Rosh Abdelfattah and Alexandria International Short Film Festival president Mohamed Mahmoud , about what actually shapes their decisions once submissions arrive.

For Abdelfattah, artistic quality is only one consideration when assembling a program. Rotterdam’s festival aims to showcase cinema from across the Arab world, meaning the volume of films produced in different countries can itself affect a selection.

“If I have a film from Sudan or a film from Egypt and they have the same level of artistic quality, and I have to choose one, I give the film from Sudan the opportunity and the stage,” he explains, since Egypt produces far more films than Sudan.

Abdelfattah is also looking for filmmakers who resist an increasingly familiar festival aesthetic. He points to the proliferation of labs, co-production programs and other development pipelines over the past decade, arguing that films can lose some of their individuality as they move through them. “In each stage, they cut something,” he observes. “They lose the personal touch.”

Navigating relationships with producers and co-producers therefore requires filmmakers to remain firm about what they are trying to make. “You have to be very, very strong to protect your vision,” he adds. “It can be very difficult.”

Mahmoud, meanwhile, sees one of the biggest problems occurring before programmers even watch submissions. Filmmakers, he argues, too often submit without determining whether a festival is suited to their work.

“A film that explores social issues might be submitted to a festival that focuses primarily on environmental themes or the natural world,” he notes. “Why submit a film to a festival that does not align with its subject matter or artistic vision?”

That makes distribution strategy increasingly central to the filmmaking process. “I believe that film distribution has become just as important as editing, cinematography, production and directing,” Mahmoud continues. Whether filmmakers distribute their own work or work with professionals, he argues that they should consider premiere strategy, a festival’s programming priorities and whether its audience is appropriate for the film rather than simply submitting as widely as possible.

Once a filmmaker has identified the right festival, Mahmoud points to more basic mistakes that can derail a submission. Filmmakers enter the wrong competition, leave required information or materials incomplete, fail to respond to festival requests or submit films that fall outside eligibility dates. “Filmmakers should carefully review the festival’s rules and requirements before submitting,” he urges.

“A film being accepted into a festival does not necessarily mean that it is a good film, nor does it mean that it is the best,” Mahmoud stresses. “Conversely, a film being rejected does not mean that it lacks quality or artistic value.”

Rotterdam Arab Film Festival’s own programming priorities differ from those of the major European festivals. Abdelfattah estimates that roughly half or more of its program comes through Arab festivals such as Cairo, Red Sea, El Gouna, Marrakech or Amman, with relatively few films sourced through Cannes, Berlin or Venice.

He also rejects the idea of a single Arab cinema. “The films from the Maghreb are different from films from Egypt,” he says, pointing to the different ways cinema has developed in Morocco, Egypt and Lebanon, for example. “We share some values, but we have different kinds of cinema.”

That distinction matters for a festival serving both Arab and Dutch audiences. Abdelfattah says Rotterdam’s audience is roughly evenly divided between the two, and films do not always land with each group in the same way. Comedy can be particularly revealing. During one screening, he remembers hearing different halves of the room laugh at different moments.

“Translating is a difficult art,” he says, noting that the challenge extends beyond language to cultural context.

For Mahmoud, a festival’s responsibility to emerging filmmakers should also extend beyond selecting and screening their work. He believes festivals should connect young filmmakers with established directors and producers while offering workshops and masterclasses where they can develop their skills and learn from people already working in the industry. “This allows young filmmakers to learn, network, gain inspiration and grow professionally,” he says.

Palestinian-Jordanian filmmaker Darin J. Sallam, director of “Farha” and a member of SIFF’s narrative feature jury this year, approaches festival decisions from the other side of the selection process. As a filmmaker who has also served on juries, she recognizes how much individual perspective shapes those decisions.

“Evaluating films is ultimately a subjective process shaped by individual perspectives and sensibilities,” Sallam says.

When judging, Sallam is less interested in comparing styles or technical accomplishments than in what remains after the screening.

“It’s about how these ideas were treated by their filmmakers and how they made us feel as jury members, and which characters and stories stayed with us when we woke up the day after,” she explains. “For me, the success of the film is related to how the film lives in people’s minds and hearts after the film is over.”

article_text:
15 August – 1 November 2026, Infosys Gallery

Pairing historical objects with modern and contemporary photographic responses, this exhibition examines Indian wrestling as a complex cultural site — tracing how ideas of strength, discipline, spectacle, body and community move across art, popular culture and lived tradition.

I will fight you for it – this is not a new sentiment, and can perhaps be traced back to an innate instinct to take by might that which we cannot easily lay claim to. Think of Bhima’s weeks-long struggle with Jarasandha in the Indian epic Mahabharata or Enkidu wrestling Gilgamesh in the ancient Sumerian Epic of Gilgamesh or the Biblical episode of Jacob wrestling the Angel in the dark; imagine the schist relief and Gandhara carvings depicting Buddha wrestling or miniatures showing wrestlers, and you may come to our long and intimate relationship with wrestling and how it has moved from royal courtyards and akharas to other surfaces and mediums – some obvious, some less so.

Once a momentous sport flourishing under patronage, in the present day, Indian wrestling is under threat. Complex struggles of gender, power, social inequity weaken a form that was already burdened by rapid technological inventions.

Imagine – the acts of grappling and rolling are wrestling’s most obvious manifestations. But, what are the things that shape and surround it? Do class, community, religion, and other threads, as well as an artist’s gaze ask us to reconsider the form?

Through a curated selection of works by celebrated photographers like the late Raghu Rai, T.S. Satyan and modernist and contemporary photographers like Jyoti Bhatt, Indrajit Khambe and Prarthna Singh, we consider the momentary and invisible that shape the historic in wrestling.

Step into MAP this August and join us outside the akhara to experience wrestling in a new way.

Sweat and Soil, #008, Indrajit Khambe, 2018 Motibag Talim, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India 35.56 cm, 53.34 cm

article_text:
エジプトのピラミッドで観光客が「80メートル」滑落！ 精鋭救急隊員による2時間の救助活動で救出｜10月19日、エジプト・ダハシュール考古学地区にあるスネフェル王の屈折ピラミッドを訪れたスペインの観光客が、内部の通路を80メートルにわたり滑落。地元の救急隊員によって助け出された。【続きを読む】 Photo: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images

中国で観光客が兵馬俑2体を破損。5メートル下の坑に飛び降り、狼藉後は地面に寝そべる｜5月30日、中国・西安市の第3号兵馬俑坑で、観光客の男が2体の兵馬俑に損傷を与える事件が起きた。当局によると、男は防護柵を乗り越え、5メートルを超える深さの坑に飛び降りたという。【続きを読む】 Photo: Kevin Frayer/Getty Images

酔った男がインカ文明期に作られた石壁を破壊。「最大限の制裁を求める」と捜査当局｜12角の石として知られるインカ文明期に作られた遺跡を酔った男がハンマーで殴打した。男の身柄はすでに確保されており、歴史的建造物の破壊の罪で、最大6年の懲役刑が言い渡される可能性がある。【続きを読む】 ペルーのクスコにあるインカ・ロカ宮殿の12角の石。Photo: Luis Rosendo/Heritage Images/Getty Images

トルコ考古学遺産「第二のカッパドキア」をカフェに無断改装!? 古代の石に電気配線、墓でコーヒー｜トルコのアフィヨンカラヒサル県にある3000年前の岩窟墓が無許可でカフェレストランに改築されていたことが分かった。【続きを読む】 3000年前の岩窟墓を改築して作られたカフェ「タシュ・バフチェ（石の庭）」。Photo: Selim Uzun/Hürriyet

「第二のカッパドキア」とも呼ばれるこの遺跡はユネスコ世界遺産暫定リストに登録されており、地元の考古学者たちは激しく非難している。 岩窟墓内でカフェを営業していた時の様子。Photo: Selim Uzun/Hürriyet

イギリス王室の伝説的遺物「運命の石」が危機一髪！ キルト姿の男性が展示ケースを襲撃するも無事｜イギリス王室に伝わる古代の戴冠石「運命の石」。7月12日、この石を特別展示中だったスコットランドのパース博物館で、35歳の男性が故意に石の保護ガラスを破壊する事件が起こった。【続きを読む】 2023年4月27日、チャールズ国王の戴冠式のため、ウェストミンスター寺院へ輸送される「運命の石」。Photo: Russell Cheyne - Pool/Getty Images

泥酔した英空軍技師がパディントン像を真っ二つに破壊。転売を試みるも失敗、有罪が確定｜イギリス・ニューベリーに設置されていたパディントンの像がイギリス空軍に所属する2人の技術者によって破壊され、持ち去られた。その後2人は起訴され、それぞれ12カ月の社会奉仕と修理費約53万円の支払いが命じられた。【続きを読む】 街中に設置されたパディントンの像。Photo: via X/@VisitNewbury

イーロン・マスク像を刃物で切りつけ？ トランプ政権とマスクに対する抗議の一環か｜インターネットミームを元に作られたイーロン・マスクの胸像が、何者かによって傷付けられていることがわかった。アメリカでは現在、トランプ政権に対する抗議の一環としてテスラの販売代理店などを狙った過激な抗議活動が相次いでおり、今回の破壊行為もその一環として行われた可能性がある。【続きを読む】 破壊されたイーロン・マスクの胸像・Photo: via X

動物愛護団体が救助か。アート作品として展示された3匹の子豚が盗まれる｜デンマーク・コペンハーゲンで行われた本物の子豚を使ったアート展示で、3月1日、生体が盗まれる事件が起こった。この作品は、子豚をケージに閉じ込めて飢え死にさせることで、同国における養豚業のずさんな管理体制を問うという内容だった。【続きを読む】 Photo: Edwin Remsberg/VW Pics/Universal Images Group via Getty Images

オランダ自治体がアート作品46点を「粗大ごみ」として処分。アンディ・ウォーホル作品も｜オランダのマースホルスト市役所が、アンディ・ウォーホルが制作した元オランダ女王ベアトリクスをモチーフにしたシルクスクリーンを含む46点の芸術作品を誤って処分していたことが分かった。【続きを読む】 ベアトリクス王女。背後には「Reigning Queens」シリーズの同王女の作品。Photo: Patrick van Katwijk/Getty images

キム・カーダシアン、誤情報の拡散をめぐる訴訟でドナルド・ジャッド財団と和解｜キム・カーダシアンが「ドナルド・ジャッドのテーブル」として紹介した家具が偽物だったとして、ドナルド・ジャッド財団はカーダシアンと家具を制作したデザイン会社を提訴していたが、6月初めに和解に達した。【続きを読む】 Photo: Taylor HillGetty Images

カニエ・ウェストが著名写真家の作品を無断使用？ 最新アルバムジャケットにKKKの「結婚式写真」｜カニエ・ウェストが最新アルバム『CUCK』のジャケット写真を公開した。その画像に使われた、KKKメンバーの「結婚式の写真」が無断使用だった可能性が浮上し、撮影者が法的措置を進めている。【続きを読む】 カニエ・ウェストが無断で使用した、ピーター・ファン＝アットマールの《The wedding of two members of the KKK in a rural America》。Photo: Peter van Agtmael/Magnum Photos

Les Braves (Coward)

Un film de Lukas Dhont

Avec Emmanuel Macchia, Valentin Campagne

Genre : Drame historique

Durée : 2h08

Note : Si le téléchargement ne fonctionne pas en cliquant directement sur un lien, veuillez cliquer avec le bouton droit sur ce lien et choisir l'option "Enregistrer la cible du lien sous..." ou "Enregistrer le lien sous..." ou "Télécharger le fichier lié sous..." suivant votre navigateur.

1916. Première guerre mondiale. Front belge. Pierre vient de rejoindre les troupes, impatient de faire ses preuves. Derrière les lignes, dans l'équipe de ravitaillement en vivres et en matériel, Francis organise des spectacles pour maintenir le moral des soldats. Alors que les combats font rage, chacun tente d’échapper à la brutalité de la guerre, ne serait-ce qu'un instant.

article_text:
Films and events

Love

Dao

The new film by Alain Gomis is a formally inventive, politically attuned meditation on the enduring ties of the African diaspora, and the meaning of family and community.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Alain Gomis

With Katy Correa, D’Johé Kouadio, Samir Guesmi

France-Senegal-Guinea-Bissau 2026. 185min

Courtesy of The Party Film Sales

Languages French, Manjak, Wolof, Creole Portuguese With English subtitles

Introduction

Moving between a memorial ritual in Guinea-Bissau and a wedding in France, Dao brings these two rites of passage into intimate conversation, exploring diasporic lives shaped by distance, memory and belonging. Blending fictional narrative with interviews and rehearsal scenes with its performers, Gomis creates a warm, richly layered, jazz-inflected portrait in which lived experience and performance continually illuminate one another.

Hyun Jin Cho

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

House of the Wind

Cameroonian director Bernard Auguste Kouemo Yanghu’s outstanding feature debut is a poignant tale of an ageing parent who has been left behind.

Masc

Bertil Nilsson’s distinctive debut follows Robin as he moves through temporary jobs and tentative relationships in search of a place to belong.

Let Them Be Seen

Nolitha Refilwe Mkulisi’s debut feature – a tender love letter to Tapoleng, her hometown in South Africa – offers an intimate evocation of a community in transition.

article_text:
Holm Friebe und Rainer Kirberg wollen Ketchup aus der Banausenecke holen. Dafür bemühen sie Kant, Warhol und die Psychoanalyse – und pressen aus der roten Soße erstaunlich viel Kulturgeschichte heraus

Die Idee ist natürlich schon wieder super. Aber das ist schließlich auch Holm Friebes Berufsbezeichnung: "Gute-Ideen-Haber", Jahrgang 1972. Oder Autor, Kunstsammler, Auktionsveranstalter und früherer Agenturbetreiber. Zuletzt hat er Kunst als Tattoos verkauft , nun hat er ein Buch zum Kochen mit Ketchup herausgebracht. Und zwar mit Filmemacher Rainer Kirberg, Jahrgang 1954.

Das Hinzufügen der zuckrigen Tomatensoße an selbstzubereitetes Essen, hat natürlich eine Banausen-Ruf, und vom selbigem wollen die beiden Popkultur-Universalgelehrten das Zeug befreien. Und zwar indem sie es erstmal in Kunst und Literatur suchen.

Doch vergebens! Bei Susan Sontag kommt er nicht vor, nicht bei Martin Parr. Nicht mal Roland Barthes hat über ihn geschrieben! Nur in der Volkswirtschaftslehre finden sie Verweise. Und sie schreiben, der metaphorische "Ketchup-Effekt" tauche auch in den Politik- und Gesellschaftswissenschaften auf: "Immer geht es dabei um das Prinzip 'Erst zu wenig, dann zu viel', das sich aus der spezifischen Viskosität ableitet, dem komplexen Wesen des Ketchups aber ansonsten nicht ansatzweise gerecht wird."

Ein wilder Ritt

Das wollen die beiden Autoren mit diesem Buch ändern. Also wird erstmal ordentlich geschüttelt. Wir lernen nicht nur, dass die ikonische Plastik-Pommesgabel EU-weit seit 2021 verboten ist, sondern tauchen auch kurz in die Geschichte des Kochens ein, treffen Gastrokritiker, denken über Distinktion nach, gar über Zivilisation! Über Nahrungsmuster, Salz, das römische Garum und woher der Name Ketchup eigentlich kommt (es gibt verschiedene Erklärungen). Und die Tomate? Woher kommt die? Natürlich geht es auch irgendwann darum, dass Ketchup für Blut steht, wofür man am besten die Psychoanalyse in die Pommes-Schale holt.

Man merkt es schon, der Ketchup-Essay ist ein wilder Ritt. Unterhaltsam. Wenig banausenhaft. Und somit das ideale Weihnachtsgeschenk für eine recht große Zielgruppe. Wenn der Essay des Buches aus dem März-Verlag auch ein wenig aufgeblasen ist. So wie der künstliche Geschmack der Soße, die vorgibt, nach Tomate zu schmecken.

Apropos Geschmack. Dazu wird natürlich Kant herangezogen: "Als gegen Ende des 18. Jahrhunderts die großen philosophischen Systeme der Ästhetik entwickelt werden, stellt Immanuel Kant in Kritik der Urteilskraft fest: Weil Geschmack eine Kategorie des Sozialen ist, wird er als guter und nicht als schöner Geschmack gefasst", heißt es an einer Stelle. Und da hat man schon fast vergessen, um was es geht, um diese Soße mit Essig und Gewürzen und Zucker und Tomaten. Und um dessen Geschmack. Friebe hat klare Vorstellungen davon, welcher Ketchup gut schmeckt. Follower konnten das bereits auf seinen Meta-Accounts verfolgen.

Alles aus dem Ketchup rausgequetscht

Doch interessant ist es schon, zu lesen, wie und wo der Ketchup entstand (wird jetzt hier nicht verraten), was die Geschichte des Erfolgs der Firma Heinz ist und was das alles mit Konservendosen zu tun hat. Man hat also wirklich alles aus diesem Ketchup rausgequetscht. Wobei, der Text umgeht fast, die Klassenfrage allzu hoch zu hängen. Denn Ketchup ließe sich ja auch Kindesverwahrlosung in Plastikflasche lesen.

Aber weil es irgendwann sogar um die Berkshire-Hathaway-Aktie geht, um die Herkunft von Pop-Art, um Beuys, um Warhol, an denen sie dann einen Kulturkonflikt namens "Ketchup vs. Honig" ausmachen, kann man den Ketchup auch gleich noch viel höher hängen, etwa wenn die Autoren ihm etwas Politisches geben wollen. Da zeigt sich dann eine etwas überholte politische Ausrichtung, die von Anti-Amerikanismus aus argumentiert. Denn natürlich ist nämlich eigentlich Hitler schuld daran, dass man den Ketchup vielleicht etwas kritisch sieht: "Hitler ließ sich von seinem Reichsbauernführer Walther Darré mit Bio-Gemüse versorgen, Himmler schwärmte für regenerative Energien, alternative Heilkunst und Anthroposophie und ließ von der SS biologisch-dynamische Versuchshöfe betreiben. Göring verordnete die ersten Tier- und Naturschutzgesetze, die von der Bundesrepublik unbesehen übernommen wurden", heißt es auf Seite 63. Und weiter: "Hinter alldem lag jene dumpfe Verklärung ländlicher und vormoderner Daseinsformen, die seit jeher auch den NS-typischen Antiamerikanismus und Antisemitismus grundiert."

Ketchupessen gegen Russland? Ketchupessen gegen Antisemitismus? Könnte jetzt auf den nächsten Seiten kommen, aber wir sind ja nicht bei der neuen deutschen Blödheit von Jörg Thadeusz oder Florian Schröder. Deswegen biegt der Essay brav noch mal zu Hela-Gewürzketchup und in den Osten ab, bevor es zum großen Ketchuptest und dann endlich zu den Rezepten kommt.

Gegenspieler Mayo

Kulturkritikerinnen Hilka Dirks, Laura Helena Wurth und Anne Waak holen kühn raus, was rauszuholen ist. Waak macht den Ketchup selbst. Ist das schon Anti-Imperialismus? Wurth rät zu einer Soße für Schlüsselkinder aus Sahne und Ketchup. Ist das schon Verwahrlosung? Und Dirks bereitet Garnelen-Cocktail zu, "21–25" Garnelen. Und das ist schon Humor.

Buchautor und Pizzaiolo Ulf Geyersbach macht Toast-Hawaii Thüringer Art. Ex-Politiker Klaus Lederer macht ein weiteres Ost-Gericht, Wurstgulasch mit Werder-Ketchup. Künstlerin Susanne Schirdewahn "kocht" einen Auflauf mit Reis, Huhn, Ketchup, Bananen und Streukäse.

Man möchte sich an dieser Stelle natürlich überhaupt nicht als Ketchup-Kritiker outen, nicht dass Söder gleich wieder den Länderfinanzausgleich streichen will. Aber meiner Meinung nach gehört Ketchup einzig und alleine an gebratene Vortags-Nudeln mit Ei. Nicht so, wie Holm Friebe es als Rezept vorschlägt, gekocht und reingespritzt. Und an Pommes kommt natürlich nur Mayonaise. Aber ich lasse lieber die Künstlerin und Autorin Olga Hohmann sprechen, die ebenfalls einen Beitrag für das Buch verfasst hat: "Eigentlich mochte ich Ketchup nie. Nur in Verbindung mit Mayonnaise. Ketchup braucht Mayo."

title_original: 【動画】「第78回 正倉院展」奈良国立博物館で11月9日まで　井上洋一館長「シルクロードの風を感じながら天平の美の世界を堪能」
editorial_title_zh: 【视频】“第78届正仓院展”将于奈良国立博物馆举行至11月9日 馆长井上洋一表示：“在感受丝绸之路清风的同时尽情领略天平美学世界”

article_text:
古都奈良の秋の風物詩「第78回 正倉院展」が10月24日開幕しました（11月9日まで会期中無休）。今年も奈良国立博物館の井上洋一館長が「シルクロードの風を感じながら天平の美の世界を堪能してほしい」と全国の美術ファンにメッセージを寄せてくれました。

奈良国立博物館館長の井上洋一さんの話

こんにちは奈良国立博物館館長の井上洋一です。今年も正倉院展の季節がやってまいりました。 第78回の正倉院展の今年も聖武天皇のご遺愛品をはじめ、素晴らしい宝物の数々をご覧いただくことができます。

そしてまた、正倉院事務所が行っております 藺筵 あるいは動物に関する調査研究、この成果もご覧いただくことができます。

シルクロードの風を感じる宝物

今回の正倉院展の見どころは やはり今ここにあります。漆胡瓶と白瑠璃瓶という2つの 胡瓶 に象徴される天平文化の国際性だろうと思います。

また会場には西方の異国の酔胡王を形どった伎楽面、中国・唐で製作されたと考えられる非常に珍しい四角の海獣葡萄鏡などが並びます。それらとともに、遥かシルクロードの彼方からこの奈良にもたらされた文化の息吹というもの、そして世界に開かれた天平の都・奈良の壮大なロマンを味わっていただけます。 シルクロードの風を感じながら、素晴らしい天平の美の世界を堪能していただければと思います。 今回も素晴らしい宝物の数々が一堂に会しております。ぜひお出掛けくださいませ。

（動画撮影・編集 読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班 岡本公樹）

正倉院展のチケットは美術展ナビチケットアプリ（スマホ）で好評発売中

第78回 正倉院展

会場：奈良国立博物館 東西新館（奈良市登大路町50 奈良公園内）

会期：2026年10月24日（土）～11月9日（月）

休館日：会期中は無休

開館時間：8:00～18:00 ※金土日祝は20時まで （入場は閉館の60分前まで）

観覧料（日時指定券）：一般2,000円（1,500円）、高大生1,500円（1,000円）、小中生500円（無料）、キャンパスメンバーズ学生400円 ※カッコ内はレイト割料金（月～木は16時以降、金～日と祝日は17時以降） 日時指定枠に空きがある場合には、博物館敷地内の特設窓口にて当日の「日時指定券」を販売するが、1枚ごとに200円の発券料がかかる。

詳しくは正倉院展公式サイト（ https://shosoin-ten.jp/ ）、 博物館公式ホームページ へ。

◇「第78回 正倉院展」（奈良国立博物館）徹底ガイド 10月24日から11月9日まで 見どころからグッズまで

Maria）的所在地，拥有世界最大的砖砌椭圆形穹顶，也是意大利国王维托里奥·埃马努埃莱三世·德·萨伏依（Vittorio Emanuele III di Savoia）与黑山王后埃莱娜（Elena del Montenegro）的安葬之地。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Landandart Carbone），请她向我们讲述与雅各布·贝纳西合作创作本届 Landandart 的缘起：“我们选择雅各布·贝纳西是因为我们喜欢他身处艺术之中的方式：直接、激进而毫不妥协。他是一位通过做减法进行创作的艺术家，其手势与语言精炼却极具张力，不需要任何装饰性效果或形式上的自满。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种敏感度让我们觉得与 VIA 的精神极为贴近。我们寻找的并非仅仅局限于融入风景的作品，而是能够与风景建立真实关系、在一瞬间改变人们对它的感知并为穿行其间的人留下点什么的介入方式。贝纳西最让我们震撼的正是这一点：他能够将一切简化至本质，在本案中即是光，并将一个简单的元素转化为强烈的体验。他的作品与我们选择的其他作品有所不同，但共同的核心需求是：不为某个地方做装饰，而是与它展开对话。”", Foo）创作一件作品。福喷泉是一处历史悠久且备受民众喜爱的喷泉，直到1900年这里一直是该村唯一的饮用水源。因此，它也是社区的聚会场所，更是隐匿于林中、用于举办户外戏剧表演的舞台。“Foo”这个词可能指的是山毛榉（faggio），但传说一位当地诗人被这个地方的魔力所迷住，想象这个名字指的是一位传说中的农牧神（Fauno）：“La funtan-na dël Faun – sota ‘l sol dël mess-dì– a l’è tuta un gioëgh bel – êd rifless verd e giaon…”，即：“农牧神的喷泉——在正午的阳光下——是一场美丽的游戏——满是绿色与黄色的倒影……”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "光的影像，没有照相机的摄影", "translated": true}, "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如评论家兼策展人安东尼奥·格鲁利（Antonio "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "喷泉重新成为相聚之所", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在开幕式期间，这座喷泉再次成为社区的聚集场所，并上演了一场行为表演。当贝纳西用扩音器吸引公众的注意力时，当地的“小游吟诗人”（“I article_text:
Al percorso Landandart si aggiunge una nuova opera. Promosso dall’associazione culturale VIA , Landandart, tra le colline del Monregalese, si inserisce in un più ampio impegno per la valorizzazione culturale e artistica del territorio e per la creazione di occasioni di incontro tra arte contemporanea, luoghi e comunità. Il percorso comprende già le opere di Emilio Ferro, Giovanni Ozzola, Carlo D’Oria e Antonio Capaccio , a cui si aggiunge ora l’installazione luminosa di Jacopo Benassi .

Artista multidisciplinare, con oltre vent’anni di ricerca sperimentale tra fotografia, performance, musica e installazioni, noto per la sua messa in discussione dei linguaggi e dei dispositivi della rappresentazione ha anche questa volta sovvertito in maniera radicale il codice della fotografia classica. Benassi ha realizzato un’installazione scultorea per Vicoforte, sede del santuario dedicato alla Natività di Maria, con la cupola ellittica in muratura più grande del mondo, e luogo di sepoltura del re d’Italia Vittorio Emanuele III di Savoia e della regina Elena del Montenegro.

Un nuovo intervento per Landandart: l’opera di Jacopo Benassi

Abbiamo chiesto a Giulia Carbone , presidente e cofondatrice dell’associazione VIA insieme a Geremia Siboni e Sergio Basso , e anima del progetto, di raccontarci come è nata la collaborazione con Jacopo Benassi per questa edizione di Landandart: «Abbiamo scelto Jacopo Benassi perché ci piace il suo modo di stare nell’arte: diretto, radicale, senza compromessi. È un artista che lavora per sottrazione, con gesti e linguaggi essenziali ma di grande forza, senza bisogno di effetti decorativi o di compiacimenti formali.

È una sensibilità che sentiamo vicina allo spirito di VIA. Non cerchiamo opere che si limitino a inserirsi nel paesaggio, ma interventi capaci di instaurare con esso una relazione autentica, di cambiarne per un momento la percezione e di lasciare qualcosa a chi lo attraversa. Con Benassi ci ha colpito proprio questo: la capacità di ridurre tutto all’essenziale, in questo caso alla luce, e di trasformare un elemento semplice in un’esperienza intensa. La sua opera è diversa dalle altre che abbiamo scelto, ma condivide con tutte la stessa esigenza: non decorare un luogo, bensì instaurare un dialogo con esso».

La Fontana del Foo, tra memoria e comunità

Jacopo Benassi è stato invitato a creare un’opera per la Fontana del Foo, un’antica e popolare fontana che fino al 1900 era l’unica fonte di acqua potabile del paese. Di conseguenza, era anche un luogo di ritrovo per la comunità e un palcoscenico immerso nel bosco per spettacoli teatrali all’aperto. La parola Foo indicherebbe probabilmente il faggio, ma la tradizione racconta che un poeta locale, incantato dalla magia del luogo, abbia immaginato che il nome si riferisse a un leggendario fauno: «La funtan-na dël Faun – sota ‘l sol dël mess-dì– a l’è tuta un gioëgh bel – êd rifless verd e giaon…», ovvero: «La fontana del Fauno – sotto il sole di mezzogiorno – è tutta un bel gioco di riflessi verdi e gialli…».

Immagine di luce, una fotografia senza macchina fotografica

Benassi parte proprio da questo luogo speciale per creare la sua opera Immagine di luce. Entrando in sintonia con l’aulicità di Vicoforte e con la tradizione del luogo, ha realizzato per la Fontana del Foo una grande installazione luminosa. Immagine di luce è una rosa monumentale, realizzata con un tronco di castagno, dalle spine rivolte verso l’alto. Alla sua estremità, una sorgente luminosa proietta un potente fascio di luce che, al calar della notte, illumina la fontana, facendola emergere dal buio del bosco.

«La fotografia è fatta di luce. Con Immagine di luce ho immaginato di eliminare tutto il resto: la macchina fotografica, la registrazione, l’archivio. Rimane soltanto la luce che appare e scompare, e l’esperienza di chi la incontra. Ogni immagine esiste solo per un attimo, senza lasciare tracce se non nella memoria di chi la vede», afferma Jacopo Benassi.

In un’epoca in cui siamo visivamente sommersi, lo scatto di Jacopo Benassi riporta l’immagine in una dimensione preziosa, quella del momento presente. L’istante viene catturato con il grande flash, senza l’uso di una macchina fotografica, e rimane sospeso in una dimensione puramente esistenziale. Benassi eleva a una dimensione sacrale il suo rapporto con la luce.

Come scrive il critico e curatore Antonio Grulli, «Da un lato ha dato un ‘corpo’ alla fotografia attraverso le sue installazioni, rendendola sempre più fisica, scultorea, imponente e al tempo stesso fragile e precaria. Dall’altro è andato nella direzione opposta, come dopo una fantastica finta, ovvero sottraendo tutto alla fotografia, la camera, la pellicola o la memoria digitale, la stampa su carta o altri supporti, riportandola a essere pura luce scorporata, onda luminosa chiamata a scrivere nel vento e nel buio per pochissimi secondi, senza lasciare alcuna traccia, ma mantenendo la propria attitudine a essere impronta, imprimitura del mondo attraverso la luce».

La fontana torna a essere un luogo di incontro

Durante l’inaugurazione, la fontana è tornata a essere un luogo di aggregazione per la comunità, diventando il teatro di una performance. Mentre Benassi richiamava l’attenzione del pubblico con il suo megafono, la banda locale “I Menestrelli” intonava le canzoni del Carnevale di Vicoforte, creando un momento di unione e condivisione che ha celebrato la nuova opera nel bosco. Immagine di luce si accenderà ogni volta che un viandante si fermerà alla fontana, invitandolo ad azionare il flash e a generare un’immagine destinata a vivere soltanto nella memoria.

Con Landandart, uno dei progetti attraverso cui l’associazione VIA promuove il dialogo tra arte contemporanea e territorio, il cammino diventa un’esperienza di scoperta, dove la bellezza del paesaggio incontra nuove letture dei luoghi e della comunità. Il percorso Landandart si sviluppa nel territorio di Vicoforte, in dialogo con il paesaggio e il patrimonio storico locale, nell’area del Santuario Basilica della Natività di Maria e lungo il sentiero Landandè.

article_text:
The National Arts Festival in Makhanda, South Africa, invites applications for an Artistic Director to lead its curatorial vision, champion emerging talent and strengthen artistic exchange across Africa and internationally. The position is offered on a five-year renewable contract.

Open Call:

The National Arts Festival (NAF) is recruiting an Artistic Director to shape the next chapter of one of South Africa’s established multidisciplinary arts festivals. The successful candidate will define the festival’s artistic vision, curatorial identity, and long-term programming strategy, positioning Makhanda as a centre for contemporary African artistic production, experimentation, and exchange. Working alongside the Chief Executive Officer, the Artistic Director will oversee artistic programming, commissioning, artist relationships, the Fringe programme, emerging artist development and international partnerships.

The role encompasses theatre, dance, music, comedy, visual arts, literature, film, digital arts and interdisciplinary practices, with an emphasis on artistic quality, cultural representation and innovation. A central responsibility will be developing new opportunities for African artists through commissions, mentorship, touring pathways and collaborations with festivals across the continent and internationally.

Institutional Context:

The National Arts Festival is a multidisciplinary cultural event held annually in Makhanda, South Africa. With a history spanning more than five decades, the festival brings together established and emerging artists working across diverse disciplines and cultural traditions. Its programming includes curated performances and exhibitions, the Fringe platform, artist development initiatives and opportunities for international cultural exchange.

The appointment supports the festival’s ambition to strengthen its position as a leading contemporary African arts festival over the next 50 years. The Artistic Director will contribute to this development by supporting new artistic production, expanding international networks and strengthening connections between the festival, its audiences and the wider cultural sector.

Eligibility and Criteria:

The festival seeks a highly networked artistic leader who can develop a distinctive curatorial vision and manage a complex multidisciplinary programme.

Applicants should demonstrate:

The ability to develop and implement a long-term artistic and curatorial strategy.

Knowledge of contemporary African artistic practices across multiple disciplines.

Strong relationships with artists, curators, cultural organisations and international networks.

Experience managing substantial budgets and taking responsibility for expenditure.

The ability to work independently and meet demanding deadlines.

Strong communication, consultation and leadership skills.

Resourcefulness in working within financial constraints.

The ability to identify partnerships and contribute to fundraising activities.

The successful candidate will also be expected to advance cultural, linguistic and demographic representation, support indigenous African artistic forms and engage with emerging technologies.

Experience in artistic commissioning, artist development, international collaboration and multidisciplinary programming will be particularly relevant to the position.

Evaluation Process:

The Artistic Director will report directly to the Chief Executive Officer and form part of the festival’s executive leadership. The role includes chairing an Artistic Committee comprising practising artists, curators and sector specialists who advise on programming, artistic recognition and quality standards.

The National Arts Festival’s Board provides strategic oversight through the Chief Executive Officer and its Artistic Programming subcommittee. Applicants should consult the full Terms of Reference for additional information.

The festival’s recruitment process is guided by its Employment Equity commitments and aims to ensure its team reflects South Africa’s diversity.

Practical Information:

Application deadline : 30 October 2026

Position: Artistic Director

Institution: National Arts Festival

Location: Makhanda, Eastern Cape, South Africa

Contract: Five-year renewable term

Reporting line: Chief Executive Officer

The appointed Artistic Director will lead the festival’s artistic programme, including its Fringe, Young Artists, and new commissioning initiatives.

Responsibilities will also include developing an NAF New Works programme, strengthening opportunities for artists to tour nationally and internationally, and contributing to an Artist Development Fund.

The role further involves collaboration with Makhanda stakeholders, including Rhodes University, on year-round creative programming, alongside initiatives to engage younger audiences and activate the festival’s archive.

Applications and Queries:

Submit applications exclusively through the National Arts Festival’s official online application form.

Applications submitted by email or through other channels will not be considered.

Applicants are encouraged to review the full Terms of Reference before submitting their applications.

Apply online: https://zfrmz.com/FcbnHB0VGuXNwpyhy1De.

Official vacancy announcement: https://nationalartsfestival.co.za/news/naf-artistic-director-vacancy/

article_text:
The Tokyo International Film Festival ‘s TIFFCOM market exhibition space sold out early this year, according to managing director Ikeda Kaori . More Japanese producers are using the Tokyo market to find partners while projects are still in development.

Last year’s edition drew more than 4,600 industry professionals from 46 countries and regions, and attendance rose 13%. Ikeda credits global interest in Japanese content for part of that growth.

Related Stories

'KPop Demon Hunters,' 'Squid Game' Stars Fete Netflix's Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases 'Tantara,' 'All of Us Are Dead' Season 2

Ava DuVernay on Her Latest Doc '14th': 'We're in the Midst of Something Very Sinister, Something Very Dangerous'

“Beyond the traditional trading of completed content, TIFFCOM has increasingly evolved into a platform for finding partners from the project development stage, leading to a significant increase in participation by Japanese producers,” Ikeda tells Variety .

She also points to Asia, which is now one of the world’s largest markets. Governments across the region are actively backing their content industries, she says.

This year’s Tokyo IP Market has grown to 10 participating IP holders and adds new categories, toys among them. The pitch event has also changed format. Each company now gives a focused pitch on its flagship IP.

The changes come after the market’s expansion to the Cannes Film Market this year, where more than 700 people registered for its pitches, panels and related programs. The audience was mostly from Europe and Hollywood. Ikeda says the IP holders who took part held a run of meetings with partners they rarely get to see in person. An initiative proposed by the Cannes market also set up matchmaking with the XR sector.

Overseas interest goes beyond the obvious hits. “IPs with an established audience, including ‘One Piece’ and ‘Super Mario,’ are undoubtedly attractive. On the other hand, Japan still possesses a great number of outstanding original works with strong potential for screen adaptations and remakes, and Tokyo IP Market is designed as the platform to discover them,” Ikeda says. Many producers want to adapt or distribute distinctive stories that are not yet well known, she adds, and each market has its own scale and audience.

The Tokyo Gap-Financing Market (TGFM) has 24 live-action and animation projects this year. It has also teamed with Canadian genre outfit Frontières. Ikeda says Japan, Thailand and Indonesia stand out in Asia for genre films such as horror and thrillers.

“Horror in particular is often deeply rooted in local culture and traditions, making it naturally unique while offering exceptional entertainment value,” she says. TGFM wants the genre focus to widen the mix of projects and filmmakers at the market. It also hopes to give Asian projects a route into North America.

The market already has results to show. Two projects developed through TGFM are at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival. “The Violinist,” which took part in 2023, won the top prize at Annecy this year. Ikeda understands that the Italian financing on “The Violinist” and the Thai financing on “Four Seasons in Java” both came from connections made at TIFFCOM.

“As a gap financing market, the primary goal is the completion of the film, and being selected for film festivals is a major initial bonus,” she says.

Japanese broadcasters feature prominently in this year’s conference program. TBS will present its partnership with Legendary Entertainment and the worldwide rollout of “Sasuke,” known overseas as “Ninja Warrior.” Nippon TV will discuss its global strategy, including a drama co-produced with South Korea. In a session run by the Broadcast Program Export Association of Japan (BEAJ), TV Tokyo will present a case study on taking IP overseas through experiential exhibitions.

“While terrestrial TV remains strong in Japan, all broadcasters are actively accelerating their global initiatives. Japanese broadcasters have always been a treasure trove of powerful IP, including formats and dramas,” Ikeda says.

For anime studios looking at international partnerships, she sees the biggest obstacle as hesitation that comes from a lack of international experience. “While language and cultural differences exist, the core issue is a shortage of talent with experience in international co-production, which in turn leads to a lack of established networks. On the flip side, however, this means there is immense room for growth,” she says. TIFFCOM is hosting a conference on international anime co-production this year, where experts will cover project structuring and financing.

Short-form drama is also growing fast in Japan. Participation from AI and data analytics companies is rising steadily, and another conference looks at trends in Japanese content through data. AGBO is giving this year’s keynote.

“In such a fast-moving environment, what holds true value is first-hand insights into how AI is being used at the cutting edge,” Ikeda says. TIFFCOM is also keen to explore using AI in its own operations.

The program also includes Taiwanese project showcases, Chinese content presentations and co-production discussions involving Brazil, Canada and Japan. Ikeda doesn’t see a conflict between TIFFCOM’s role as the main marketplace for Japanese content and its goal of becoming a hub for Asia. She calls them two essential pillars.

“Southeast Asia in particular is experiencing rapid growth in both economic strength and production capabilities, alongside rising demand for Japanese content. As buyers in each country grow their domestic businesses, their opportunities to acquire Japanese content will also expand,” she says.

Ikeda doesn’t want to narrow TIFFCOM to a single next area. Instead, she wants it to keep adapting as trends and formats change, and to add partnerships with other markets and events along the lines of the Cannes collaboration.

“The content industry five years from now holds so much potential that it cannot yet be defined – and that is precisely what makes it so exciting,” she says.

"日本广播公司在今年的会议节目中表现出色,TBS将与传奇娱乐和“萨苏克”的全球角色展展展出合作伙伴关系,海外称为“忍者战士”。Nippon TV将讨论其全球战略,包括与韩国共同制作的戏剧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“虽然地面电视在日本仍然很强大,但所有广播公司都在积极加快其全球举措,日本广播公司一直是强大的IP,包括格式和戏剧的宝藏。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“虽然语言和文化差异存在,核心问题是缺乏在国际合作生产经验的天赋,这反过来导致缺乏建立的网络,但是,这意味着有巨大的增长空间,”她说。TIFFCOM今年举办了关于国际动画合作生产的会议,专家将讨论项目结构和融资。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "简形戏剧也在日本迅速增长,人工智能和数据分析公司的参与不断增加,另一场会议通过数据观察日本内容的趋势。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“在这种快速移动的环境中,真正的价值是对人工智能如何在顶端使用的第一手洞察,”Ikeda说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该计划还包括台湾项目展览、中国内容演示和涉及巴西、加拿大和日本的合作生产讨论,伊基达没有看到TIFFCOM作为日本内容的主要市场场所和其目标成为亚洲中心之间的冲突。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“特别是东南亚正在经历经济强度和生产能力的快速增长,以及日本内容的需求日益增长,随着各国的买家国内业务的增长,他们获得日本内容的机会也将扩大,”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ikeda不想将TIFFCOM紧缩到一个单一的下一个区域,而她希望它继续适应趋势和格式的变化,并在戛纳合作线沿着其他市场和活动的合作伙伴关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“五年后,内容行业拥有如此多的潜力,以至于它还无法定义 - 这正是它如此令人兴奋的原因,”她说。", "translated": true}]
excerpt_original: The Tokyo International Film Festival’s TIFFCOM market exhibition space sold out early this year, according to managing director Ikeda Kaori. More Japanese producers are using the Tokyo market to find partners while projects are still in development. Last year’s edition drew…
translated_title_zh: 日本制造商推动东京市场增长,展览空间出售
translated_excerpt_zh: 东京国际电影节的TIFFCOM市场展览空间今年早些时候出售,据导演Ikeda Kaori表示,更多日本制片人正在使用东京市场寻找合作伙伴,而项目仍在开发中。

title_original: Victor Ehikhamenor: What Remains When a City Disappears?
editorial_title_zh: 维克托·埃希卡梅诺：当城市消失时，还剩下什么？
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在悉尼大学周泽荣博物馆的佩内洛普画廊，尼日利亚裔美国艺术家兼作家维克托·埃希卡梅诺将废弃物品与日常生活碎片转化为对流离失所、文化记忆以及 […] 的深刻冥思
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "在悉尼大学周泽荣博物馆的佩内洛普画廊，尼日利亚裔美国艺术家兼作家维克托·埃希卡梅诺将废弃物品与日常生活碎屑转化为一场关于流离失所、文化记忆以及家园永恒意义的冥思。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "城市可以抹去整片街区，却无法轻易磨灭其中凝聚的生活、记忆与历史。一面被丢弃的镜子、一件穿旧的衣服、一个废弃的抽屉——这些曾是某人日常生活不可或缺部分的物品，成为了强烈提醒人们何谓失落、被带走或在别处重构的物证。对于尼日利亚裔美国艺术家兼作家维克托·埃希卡梅诺（Victor Ehikhamenor）而言，这些日常生活残余物承载着流离失所的情感分量以及归属感的持久绵延。在他的首次澳大利亚个展《解构城市：构筑家园》（Undoing the City: Making Home）中，他将悉尼、开罗和哈科特港不断变化的城市景观交织对话，揭示出旧改、移民与环境退化不仅重塑了人们居住的地方，也重塑了他们对自身身份的理解。维克托·埃希卡梅诺，《神圣之夜》（2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Victor-Ehikhamenor-_Numinous-Night_-back-front-2026-image-courtesy-Chau-Chak-Wing-Museum-773x1030-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "维克托·埃希卡梅诺，《神圣之夜》（2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "基于两年合作研究的积累，埃希卡梅诺创作了一些装置作品，其中个人记忆与移民、殖民贸易以及环境变迁的宏大历史相交织。诸如《乌瓦乌瓦》（Uwa Uwa）、《他走了》（He Left）和《不在家》（Not Home）等作品探讨了房屋与家园的区别，探究了伴随人们跨越地理界限的文化习俗、人际关系与记忆。他在尼日利亚埃多州的成长经历滋养了一种艺术语言，使其日常材料能够与精神指引和传承下来的传统共存。其创作的核心是一个简单的观察：“你不会带着房子旅行，但你会带着家旅行。”在与苏泽特·贝尔-罗伯茨（Suzette Bell-Roberts）的这次访谈中，埃希卡梅诺反思了普通物品中蕴含的历史、归属感的复杂性，以及他与悉尼西部新锐非洲裔侨民创意工作者们的交流。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "苏泽特·贝尔-罗伯茨：《解构城市：构筑家园》探讨了城市转型、流离失所与归属感。是什么吸引你关注这些主题，它们又是如何塑造你对这次展览的处理方式的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "维克托·埃希卡梅诺：让我感兴趣的问题是，当我们居住的地方开始发生变化时，我们对家园的理解会遭遇什么。城市从来都不是静态的。它在不断演变，有时通过自然过程，有时通过开发建设，有时则通过环境退化与资源开采。但当这些变化发生时，我们不得不问，那些围绕着这些地方建立生活的人们将会怎样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这次展览源自两位教授长期在不同地点（包括尼日尔三角洲的奥克里卡）开展的研究。我的角色是介入这一研究，并思考如何将其中的问题转化为一种艺术体验。我特别感兴趣的是物理上的流离失所与人们在离开一个地方时（无论是有意识还是无意识地）随身携带的事物之间的关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这引导我超越物理建筑去思考家园。我开始使用日常生活用品、二手衣物以及其他能够唤起在某地生活、离开某地并试图在别处立足之体验的材料。我不想生搬硬套地去图解研究，而是希望创作这样一个装置：通过物品、空间以及它们可能唤醒的记忆，让人切身经历这些问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览汇集了悉尼、开罗和哈科特港的经验，这些城市有着截然不同的历史和文化认同。其中浮现出了哪些联系与差异，它们又是如何为作品的发展提供养分的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我认为将这些地方汇聚在一起的趣味之处在于，你会开始看到不同的历史如何引导我们走向相似的问题。这项研究在文化、环境和政治环境大相径庭的地方之间建立了联系。我并没有亲自在所有这些地方进行实地考察。尽管如此，我对尼日利亚的熟悉——尤其是尼日尔三角洲以及围绕流离失所和资源开采的更广泛问题——为我如何回应这项研究提供了基础。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "例如，在奥克里卡，二手衣物的历史与旧货的流通开启了一场关于贸易、殖民遭遇以及物资跨越边境流动的对话。在悉尼，我收集了二手物品来构建一个关于家园与流离失所的装置。这里存在着一种有趣的联系：那些已经在某个地方生活过、被其他人使用过的物品，在进入新环境时获得了另一种生命。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当然，这些地方的历史并非可以互换。每个地方都有其自身的特殊境况，重要的是不能抹平这些差异。但是，当你审视人们如何与他们的家园建立联系、他们在搬迁时铭记什么、又携带了什么时，你就会开始认识到某些共同的人类体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对我而言，展览的核心在于让这些历史彼此对话，而不强求它们千篇一律。正因为差异依然存在，这些联系才变得意义非凡。维克托·埃希卡梅诺，《迄今》（2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Victor-Ehikhamenor-_so-far-1-773x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "维克托·埃希卡梅诺，《迄今》（2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "家（home）的概念超越了物理结构，延伸至记忆、身份和文化归属。你是如何理解“家”的，这种理解又是如何通过你的艺术实践不断演变的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们家乡有句俗语，说你出门不带房子，但你随身带着家。我想这很好地捕捉到了其中的真谛。房子是一个物理结构，但家要复杂得多。它关乎你周围的人、你的记忆、你吃的食物、你说的语言，以及塑造你自我认知的所有经历。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在埃多州成长的经历中，某些记忆和现实会一直伴随着你，无论你最终落脚何处。你可能会离开村子或搬到另一个国家，但你依然会携带这种成长的种种面相。人们在迁移时，往往会寻找同乡，重现熟悉的仪式，制作熟悉的食物，并建立起能够体验某种原初生活碎片的空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种理解启发了装置作品《Uwa Uwa》（意为“家就是家”）。通过日常物品和熟悉的材料，我探讨了人们如何在物理环境与故乡迥异的地方重构归属感。装置的其他部分，包括《他走了》（He Left）和《不在家》（Not Home），则探讨了离别、缺席以及试图在某地获得归属的种种暧昧性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我认为我的艺术实践让我越来越意识到，家并不总是一个我们可以清晰定义的概念。有时它是一个地方，有时它是一段记忆，有时则是我们仍在努力找回或重建的一种感觉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你的作品经常汲取历史悠久的贝宁王国的视觉与精神传统。在本次展览中，这些传统是如何影响你对文化记忆和不断变化的城市景观的探索的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我在埃多州的成长经历一直影响着我观察和解读世界的方式。你无法简单地将自己与塑造了你的视觉传统、文化习俗和历史割裂开来。它们已然融入你的感知力之中，即便你正在处理超越你即时文化环境的题材也是如此。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这次展览中，这些影响与那些诉说着日常生活、移民和流离失所的材料及母题并置在一起。例如，彩色玻璃下方的护身符承载着文化与精神上的联结，对某些观众来说可能一眼就能辨认，而对其他人则较为陌生。我希望这些不同的参考系能够在装置中共存，而不是把一切都解释得清清楚楚。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，我不会说这个展览仅仅关乎贝宁王国的传统。它是在对更广泛的研究做出回应，而我自身的文化背景只是我带入这一对话的视角之一。问题在于，我们如何将我们的历史带入新的环境，以及这些历史如何继续塑造我们对归属感的理解。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对我而言，文化记忆并非只存在于过去。它继续在现在发挥作用，存在于我们保留的物品、我们践行的仪式以及我们在陌生空间中赋予意义的方式之中。这种延续性塑造了我对待作品的方式。维克托·埃希卡梅诺尔，《解构城市》（2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Victor-Ehikhamenor-_Undoing-the-city-1-773x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "维克托·埃希卡梅诺尔，《解构城市》（2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在你的艺术实践中，你一直使用玫瑰经念珠、打孔纸、青铜和具象意象。你如何看待物质、记忆与叙事之间的关系，这些元素在《解构城市：构筑家园》中又扮演了什么角色？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我想首先要理解的是，材料在进入一件艺术品之前就已经有了生命。在艺术家决定拿它们做什么之前，它们就已经拥有了历史、联结和用途。我感兴趣的是，当你把某样东西从它熟悉的环境中移出并放到别处时会发生什么，这能让它获得新的意义，而不必完全失去它先前承载的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《解构城市：构筑家园》很大一部分是由二手物品制成的。当我在悉尼寻找材料时，我对那些已经被人使用过、带有历史痕迹的东西很感兴趣。一个抽屉、一条领带、一面镜子或一件普通的家居用品可能看起来微不足道，但这些物品可以包含日常生活的痕迹。它们能让我们想起特定的人、家和经历。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些材料也与我们与之相连的历史息息相关。例如，奥克里卡（Okrika）的概念将二手货的流通引入了对话。物品在不同地方之间流转，承担不同的用途，并获得新的生命。从这个意义上说，材料本身就参与了叙事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我对待一件物品时，脑海中未必已经固定了单一的意义。有时，它的重要性是在与它合作的过程中，并在思考它与装置中其他元素的关系时才显现出来的。我感兴趣的是创造这样一种情境：材料能够通过其物质存在、历史以及它在观众心中唤起的联结来诉说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这次展览源于对经历重大城市变迁的社区的合作研究。你是如何看待这些社区的故事和经历的，是什么引导你将它们转化为艺术形式的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我的出发点是参与已经开展的研究，并思考如何通过我自己的艺术感悟来做出回应。这项研究涵盖了不同的地点和经历，我并没有以仿佛能直接代表所代表的每一个社区的姿态来筹备展览。相反，我专注于可以通过材料、记忆和居住空间体验来探索的问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我不断回想并认识到，不同的人对流离失所的体验各不相同，但围绕它的情感却能在这些差异中产生共鸣。你或许并未在别人的社区生活过，也没有经历过他们完全相同的遭遇。尽管如此，你依然能够体会到对家的渴望、离去的焦虑，或是想要保留自己所熟悉的生活片段的愿望。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种理解指导了我对材料的选择。我使用了原本就是人们生活一部分的物品，将它们与绘画和其他元素结合在一起，构建出一个既能暗示家的亲密感、又能引发对缺席和错位之思考的环境。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在什么该放进展览的问题上，我也做出了实践层面和概念层面的抉择。我收集或考虑制作的东西，并非全部最终都进入了装置之中。我必须思考不同的元素是如何协同作用的，以及它们是否有助于我试图探索的问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "更重要的是，我希望作品对各种不同的诠释保持开放。这个装置借鉴了特定的研究和历史，但也为观众将自身的经历带入这种接触留出了空间。维克托·埃希卡梅诺尔（Victor Ehikhamenor），《解构城市》（Undoing the City，2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Victor-Ehikhamenor-_Undoing-the-city-2-773x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "维克托·埃希卡梅诺尔（Victor Ehikhamenor），《解构城市》（Undoing the City，2026年）。图片由周泽荣博物馆提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在展览之余，你还通过与布莱克敦艺术中心（Blacktown Arts）合作开发的一个项目，在西悉尼指导新兴的非洲及非洲后裔创意工作者。这种交流为你的艺术实践、社区观念以及跨代知识传递带来了什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我一直坚信指导是一个相互的过程。你走进一个房间时，可能被认为是那个本该分享知识的人，但这并不意味着你是唯一拥有东西可奉献的人。你必须甘愿向你所指导的人学习。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": Gallery）展出。", "links": [{"text": "Penelope Gallery", "url": "https://www.sydney.edu.au/museum/whats-on/exhibitions/undoing-the-city.html"}], "translated": true}]
